payload.name: Extract nicknames from direct-address phrases
payload.description: When a message contains a direct address or variant of a person's name, use it to record a nickname relationship before adding other facts.
content: During extraction, treat direct-address phrases (greetings, sign-offs, in-line addresses) as evidence for relationship facts, not as conversational filler.

When a speaker explicitly addresses another participant using a shortened or alternative form of their name, create a `relationship` memory stating that the speaker uses that nickname for the other person.
Emit the nickname relationship as its own candidate even when the same message contains a more salient event or state, so the address fact is not lost.

solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction focused on a salient event and dropped a nickname encoded in a direct-address phrase. This is a reusable mechanism because direct-address name variants are common evidence for relationship facts; future questions may ask what one person calls another. The rule applies whenever messages contain greetings or addresses with abbreviated or alternative names.
